prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Operating and Financial Metrics (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 92px · one-line width 452px
  col 2: header "FY 2022" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "FY 2023" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 69px
  col 4: header "FY 2024" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Q1 2025" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 557px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 556px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Track six operating and financial metrics across FY 2022–FY 2024 and Q1 2025 so readers can assess trends and current performance.","reading":"Readers identify the metric in the row header, then scan the four period columns left to right. Comparison happens horizontally within each row and vertically across metrics, so both row-label readability and period alignment matter.","groups":["FY 2022, FY 2023 and FY 2024 form a historical annual series and should share a consistent width and rhythm.","Q1 2025 is the latest/current period; it belongs with the other periods but can be treated as a distinct endpoint.","The Metric column has a separate row-label role and needs enough width to keep labels scannable."],"keep_intact":["All numeric values and units: 112%, 71.3%, 38.2%, $1,840, $318.4M, $41.2M.","Period headers FY 2022, FY 2023, FY 2024 and Q1 2025 on one line where possible.","No breaking of currency amounts, percentages or identifiers."],"may_wrap":["Long Metric labels at word boundaries, especially 'Sales and marketing expense as a percentage of revenue', 'Net revenue retention, trailing twelve months', 'Customer acquisition cost, blended', 'Annual recurring revenue, end of period' and 'Free cash flow, trailing twelve months'."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [202, 88, 90, 85, 91] · table 557×461px · row heights [66, 66, 39, 92, 66, 66, 66] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [180, 94, 94, 94, 94] · table 557×593px · row heights [39, 92, 66, 118, 92, 92, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [156, 100, 100, 100, 100] · table 557×645px · row heights [39, 118, 66, 145, 92, 92, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

Your previous reply was rejected: no JSON in reply. Reply again with ONLY the JSON object.
